clue.text: Bring in a worker carrying great weight

parts.note: to bring goods in from abroad is to import them
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A labourer is hired to haul a very heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weighty or significant in influence is described as being of great consequence.

clue.text: Might sound like very little money

indicators.note: the clue tells us the word Might is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: might is strength or power, said the same as the tiny coin word

explanation.surface: A speculation that something could be worth only a pittance.
explanation.definitionFit: The widow's mite in the Bible is a coin of tiny value, hence a small sum.

clue.text: Make work — for the after-care ward presumably

definitions.meaning: to run a machine, cause it to function
patients in a recovery ward are there post-surgery, so the ward is named for what surgeons do

explanation.definitionFit: To run a machine is to make it work; surgeons perform surgery before patients go to the post-op recovery ward.

clue.text: They try out bed canopies

definitions.meaning: people who trial or examine things
a tester is the canopy over a four-poster bed

explanation.definitionFit: Examiners trial things; a tester is also an old word for the overhead canopy of a four-poster bed.

clue.text: Point one minus point one

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass
taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of decimal arithmetic: one tenth subtract one tenth.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: 0.1 take away 0.1 leaves nothing at all, while 'Point one' also builds the letters as a compass point plus ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtracting a number from itself leaves zero, that is, not any.

clue.text: Secret international agreement by which property may be sold

definitions.meaning: a pact between nations kept confidential

definitions.text: by which property may be sold
definitions.meaning: a sale of a house negotiated directly between buyer and seller, not by auction

explanation.definitionFit: A confidential pact between states; in property, a sale agreed privately rather than at public auction.

clue.text: They sit on a pile, not caring where they stand so long as they get a seat

definitions.text: They sit on a pile, not caring where they stand so long as they get a seat

parts.words: They sit on a pile, not caring where they stand so long as they get a seat
parts.note: the pile is a pile carpet with a travelling bag on it, and the seat is a parliamentary seat won by outsiders from anywhere

explanation.definitionFit: Opportunist politicians standing in constituencies where they have no roots, named after Northern opportunists in the post-Civil War American South.

clue.text: Solicitors who married one another's sisters?

definitions.text: Solicitors who married one another's sisters?

parts.words: Solicitors who married one another's sisters?
parts.note: lawyers are literally siblings working in the law, and marrying each other's sisters makes them related by marriage too

explanation.definitionFit: Men related through marriage, as a spouse's male sibling, here punned on fellow lawyers.

clue.text: Spun fencing?

parts.note: split the first word as S plus a joke on words, and add that letter to verbal punning to get a sport of blades

explanation.definitionFit: Fencing is the sport of fighting with blades, and adding S to verbal punning gives the same term.

clue.text: It is opposed to customs dealing with priceless goods

definitions.text: It is opposed to customs dealing with priceless goods

parts.words: It is opposed to customs dealing with priceless goods
parts.note: customs means import duties; priceless goods are ones with no tariff charge added, commerce without duties

explanation.definitionFit: Commerce between countries without tariffs or import duties, the opposite of protectionism.

clue.text: Dockside farewell anticipating what is to come?

definitions.text: Dockside farewell anticipating what is to come?

parts.words: Dockside farewell anticipating what is to come?
parts.note: a hand gesture of goodbye from the quay, and also the swell of the sea the passenger will meet

explanation.definitionFit: Waving the hand says goodbye; at sea a swell or breaker is what the departing ship will meet.

clue.text: Bet he's a chap who works for payment

definitions.meaning: a stake on an outcome

definitions.text: he's a chap who works for payment
definitions.meaning: read jokily as someone earning a wage, a wage-earner

explanation.definitionFit: A bet is a stake; jokily, one who earns a weekly pay packet.

clue.text: Boxwood rafter

definitions.meaning: read as box and wood: to ... is to box, and a ... is a wooden pole
a roof beam

explanation.definitionFit: Boxers practise by sparring; a spar is a stout wooden pole such as a ship's mast or roof timber.

clue.text: Motto of the machine-gun company

definitions.meaning: a saying or principle
Hiram ... firm made the ... machine gun

explanation.definitionFit: A pithy saying of principle; also the inventor Hiram Maxim's machine-gun firm.

clue.text: Made a song about one courting another?

indicators.note: the sung word is wrapped around the next piece, so about signals a container

parts.note: made a song means sang, past participle sung
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone serenaded their beloved while wooing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside SUNG; 'courting' is a punning definition, since a suitor pleads in court as well as in love.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor woos a lover, and also brings a lawsuit, both senses of pressing a suit.

clue.text: Leading artist to copy a drawing depicting the yuppie way of life

parts.note: an RA, Royal Academician, is one of Britain's leading artists
to trace is to copy a drawing through thin paper

explanation.surface: A top painter sketches a scene showing ambitious young professionals.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The competitive struggle for career success associated with ambitious 1980s urban professionals.

clue.text: How to sink a vessel that carries coal

definitions.meaning: to sink one's own ship deliberately by holing it
a coal bucket by the fireplace

explanation.definitionFit: Crews deliberately sink their own ship by holing it; also a metal bucket for fireside coal.

clue.text: Placing — a ball in a hole?

definitions.meaning: setting something down
on the golf green, striking the ball gently into the cup

explanation.definitionFit: Setting something down; in golf, the gentle stroke on the green that rolls the ball into the cup.

clue.text: King George incurred wrath of an 18th century biographer

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's royal cipher
wrath is fury, anger

explanation.surface: A monarch made a historian furious.
explanation.walkthrough: James Granger compiled a Biographical History of England (1769).
explanation.definitionFit: James Granger was an English clergyman who wrote a celebrated biographical history in the 1760s.

clue.text: Truce an organisation arranged between man and horse

indicators.note: the letters are to be organised and set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A peace deal is brokered by a body mediating between a rider and mount.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature of Greek myth with a human upper body on a horse's legs, half one and half the other.

clue.text: Not a far reaching agreement

definitions.meaning: small and closely packed, not extensive
a pact or treaty

explanation.definitionFit: Neatly small and dense, not sprawling; also a formal pact between parties.

clue.text: Tip given by a primate with a St. Andrew's cross

parts.note: an ape is a primate
the saltire of St Andrew is X-shaped

explanation.surface: Advice offered by a monkey bearing Scotland's national emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: St Andrew's cross is the diagonal saltire on Scotland's flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A peak or summit is the highest point, the very top.

clue.text: Diary of 1939/45" hots things up

parts.note: the years of the Second World War
MS, manuscript, a handwritten record such as a diary

explanation.surface: A wartime journal makes events heat up.
explanation.definitionFit: To heat something is to raise its temperature, make it hotter.

clue.text: The old folk included in a wage demand

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words a wage demand

explanation.surface: Pensioners are covered in a pay claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly people as a group are collectively called this, as in care of the elderly.

clue.text: Picture a childish card game

definitions.meaning: a quick photograph
the children's game of calling out when two matching cards appear

explanation.definitionFit: A quick photograph or snapshot; also a children's game of matching cards.

clue.text: In Norse mythology a god, though in America a king

parts.note: tho is the American spelling of though
R, rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A note on a deity of the Norse that becomes a monarch in the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse god of thunder who wields a hammer.

clue.text: Here song-parts are arranged for office girls

indicators.note: song parts being arranged suggests rearranging these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Musical parts are scored for a choir of secretaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are arranged' shuffles the thirteen letters of HERE SONG-PARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorthand typists in an office were once mostly young women.

clue.text: Phoenician plea to Alexander in 322 BC carried by a prudent motorist

definitions.text: Phoenician plea to Alexander in 322 BC
definitions.meaning: the Phoenician city of Tyre begging Alexander the Great to spare it during his siege
an extra wheel kept in the boot

explanation.definitionFit: Tyre was a Phoenician city besieged by Alexander; drivers keep an extra wheel in the boot for punctures.
